summary: Dedicated pool: sudden p99 latency degradations correlated with GPU PCIe saturation and tenant IO-wait
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (DataMuse Analytics) reported an abrupt increase in p99 generation latency and throughput degradation for routes pinned to their dedicated GPU pool. The degradation started around 2026-03-13T09:10 UTC and manifested as frequent 1.5–3x p99 spikes, occasional 5xx errors, and increased queue lengths on the pool scheduler.

Impact:
- Affected workloads: low-latency streaming and short-completion generations for two production models (gpt-open-xxl-8k, rw-6b-quantized).
- Observed ~30% drop in sustained throughput for the pool and client-visible p99 jumping from ~220ms to ~750ms intermittently.
- Customer-facing: user-facing errors for ~7% of requests during outage windows.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-usa-east-12, region us-east-1.
- Node types: A100-40GB instances with multi-tenant process isolation.
- Runtime: serving-runtime v2.14.1.
- Autoscaling policy: predictive with burst reserve enabled.

Timeline / Observations:
- 2026-03-13 09:10 UTC: First alert from monitoring (p99 > 700ms).
- 2026-03-13 09:12 UTC: CS notified customer and opened ticket.
- 2026-03-13 09:20–09:45 UTC: Patterned p99 spikes coincident with elevated host IO wait and GPU PCIe errors in kernel logs on 2 nodes.
- 2026-03-13 10:05 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied (migrate high-latency tenants off two affected nodes).

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. Replay short-context streaming traffic at similar QPS on a test pool with identical autoscale settings.
2. Introduce concurrent small independent streams from 100 tenants with high small-IO footprint (simulated).
3. Monitor kernel dmesg for GPU PCIe errors and host iostat for high %iowait.

Logs & metrics collected:
- Serving runtime traces: increased scheduling latency between enqueue->start (median 18ms -> 60ms).
- Node-level syslogs: repeated "GPU: pcie link retrain" and "nvidia: GPU crash kernel dump" entries on node-a03 and node-a07 (timestamps aligned to p99 spikes).
- iostat: sustained device util for /dev/nvme0n1 spiking to 90% with iowait rising from 2% to 35% during incidents.
- Prometheus: GPU utilization was not saturated (avg 42%) - but PCIe errors correlate with p99.

Triage notes / hypotheses:
- Primary hypothesis: a noisy tenant (or background job) is causing heavy host-side small-block IO resulting in NVMe queue saturation; that in turn correlates with repeated GPU PCIe link retrains and transient kernel-level GPU errors, leading to temporary availability hiccups and scheduler queue amplification. This matches observed high iowait, kernel PCIe errors, and low GPU compute saturation.
- Alternate hypothesis: intermittent firmware regression on a subset of nodes causing PCIe link instability (would explain localized nodes with kernel messages).
- Less likely: serving-runtime bug in KV cache eviction causing pathological disk writes; initial traces do not show abnormal write amplification from runtime.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Isolated two nodes (node-a03, node-a07) and drained tenant slots; customer traffic migrated to warm spare nodes. This reduced p99 to ~260ms and eliminated 5xxs for the customer by 2026-03-13 10:30 UTC.
- Applied temporary QoS at host level to deprioritize tenant background IO on the affected nodes (preliminary kernel-level cgroup adjustment).

Investigation actions in-flight:
- SRE to run full nvme SMART and PCIe link diagnostics on both nodes (ticket INT-4021 tracking hardware checks).
- Runtime team to audit recent node firmware and NVIDIA driver rollouts in us-east (PRs and rollouts referenced).
- Capacity team to review autoscaler behavior and whether predictive burst allowed re-pinning that caused imbalance.
- Replayed telemetry and collected flamegraphs of scheduler queuing during incidents.

Workaround for customer:
- Recommend pinning critical routes to alternate dedicated pool or enabling fallback routing to dedicated-fallback region while investigation continues. Customer accepted temporary migration.

Next steps and owner assignments:
- [SRE] (Liam Chen) complete hardware diagnostics on node-a03/a07 and report by 2026-03-14 18:00 UTC.
- [Runtime] audit (Priya Rao) to validate no write-amplifying regressions in serving-runtime v2.14.1 by 2026-03-15.
- [Capacity/Allocator] (Marco Silva) to evaluate autoscaler logs for rebalancing behavior and propose a mitigation to prevent colocating IO-heavy tenants by 2026-03-16.
- [Customer Success] (Olivia Park) to coordinate customer communication and confirm acceptance of pool migration and timeline.

Notes for postmortem:
- Collect kernel oops, PCIe link error counters, nvme latencies, and cgroup IO metrics for the full event window.
- Determine whether host-level QoS policy should be default for dedicated nodes to protect GPU stability.
- If hardware faults confirmed, schedule replacement and consider rolling firmware updates with a smaller blast radius.

Current status: traffic restored to customer via migration. Root cause not confirmed; hardware diagnostics and runtime audit ongoing.
